description:
Found by specled_-dn4.5 cold re-verification (2026-07-25T18:24:48Z, Note 1). Under bare 'mix spec.check' the tagged_tests verification leg intermittently red-lights on three tests — test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs:1452, :1681 and test/specled_ex/review_test.exs:135 — when the machine is loaded. All three passed on an immediate re-run and in isolation. Not attributable to dn4.5.

This is a THIRD flake class in this codebase's gate path, after specled_-ya8 (async code-server mutation, FIXED) and specled_-zr6 (StreamData generator space, open). Unlike zr6 it is load-sensitive rather than seed-sensitive, so it strikes exactly when the machine is busy — i.e. during parallel orchestration, which is when a red gate is most expensive.

Fix direction: serialize these three or widen their timing budget; commits c478563 (ya8) and d300c21 already hardened neighboring tests and are the pattern to follow.

Out of the dn4 epic (pre-existing; no gate blocked). If it red-lights two dn4 merge gates it should be escalated in like ya8 was.

comments.text:
New data point for this flaky class, observed 2026-07-25 while working specled_-cz0 on branch specled_-cz0/spec-honesty.

`mix spec.check` failed once in five runs, same session, no edits between runs:

  validate status=fail errors=1 warnings=0
  [ERROR] specled.package verification_command_failed .spec/specs/package.spec.md ::
    Verification command failed: tagged_tests: mix test --include integration ...
  failing tests: test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:255
  spec.check result=fail tier=validate error_findings=1

Adds a file to this ticket's list, which so far names verifier_test.exs:1452/:1681 and review_test.exs:135.

What did NOT reproduce it (all green, exit 0):
  - mix test (full, no --include) x3
  - mix test --include integration (full suite)
  - mix test --include integration test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs (isolated)
  - mix spec.check x4 (the other four of the five)

Detail worth noting for whoever picks this up: line 255 is not a test declaration in that file. The tests bracket it at 250 ("a fabricated, unmarked finding code IS flagged") and 256/257 ("the evidence/* and cross_field/* families are guarded in both directions"); 255 is blank. Whatever emits the `failing tests:` line is reporting a line that does not correspond to a test declaration, which may be a lead on the reporting path rather than on the tests themselves.

Mechanism ruled out: a cwd race against the lint's relative corpus globs (`.spec/**/*.md`, `docs/**/*.md`). The only three File.cd! sites in the suite — binding_test.exs, coverage_closure_test.exs, spec_check_test.exs — are all async: false and carry comments saying exactly why, and ExUnit does not overlap sync modules with async ones.

The two tests bracketing line 255 are pure-constant assertions with no filesystem or process access, so neither can be load-sensitive on its own.

IMPLEMENTED
Session: 0a000e53-c6f4-4a90-9dbd-92b67b44eaf1
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-remembers/projects/-Users-mz-src-specled-ex/0a000e53-c6f4-4a90-9dbd-92b67b44eaf1.jsonl

Commit: d032ff0 (branch specled_-odl/load-fragile-tagged-tests)
Files touched: test/test_helper.exs, test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs, test/specled_ex/review_test.exs
Tests added: none (test-infrastructure hardening of existing tests)
Verification stubs flipped: none
Verification tier: change-scoped — mix test --include integration on verifier_test.exs + review_test.exs + docs_identifier_lint_test.exs (92 tests, 0 failures), mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted, mix spec.check --no-run-commands (result=pass with Spec-Drift: test_only trailer); full-system proof deferred to the merge gate / PR CI
Final-tier runs: 1

Summary: Three defenses against the load-flake class: (1) suite per-test ExUnit timeout 60s -> 120s in test_helper.exs — under orchestration load, subprocess-heavy tests slow far more than CPU-bound ones and the 60s kill converted machine load into red gates; the leg's 400s command budget still bounds real hangs. (2) The seven timeout-classification shim budgets in verifier_test.exs consolidated into @timeout_shim_budget_ms and widened 2000ms -> 4000ms (d300c21's spawn-race margin, doubled after the 1681 observation beat it). (3) ReviewTest serialized (async: false) to keep its per-test git spawns out of the async phase's fork burst, per c478563's pattern. Costs ~20s of bare spec.check runtime; cheap tiers unaffected.

Mechanism note: no failure output was ever captured from the observed flakes, so the mechanism is inferred (ExUnit 60s kill / spawn-latency race / fork pressure all fit; a 6-iteration synthetic-load repro at ~2x slowdown stayed green). The docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:255 reporting anomaly (line maps to no test declaration) could not be explained by the descriptor path, which only emits ExUnit declaration lines — follow-up specled_-td7 adds self-identifying descriptors (event id alongside file:line) and recommends setting SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR in gate environments so the next occurrence is diagnosable.

VERIFY: FAIL
Session: 0a000e53-c6f4-4a90-9dbd-92b67b44eaf1
Log: /Users/mz/.claude-remembers/projects/-Users-mz-src-specled-ex/0a000e53-c6f4-4a90-9dbd-92b67b44eaf1.jsonl

Mechanical checks:
- Files touched: 3 (test/test_helper.exs, test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs, test/specled_ex/review_test.exs)
- Files outside Allowed globs: 0 — old-style ticket with no formal Allowed-touches globs; judged against ticket prose (names verifier_test.exs, review_test.exs; fix direction 'serialize these three or widen their timing budget'). test_helper.exs is not named but is the suite-wide instrument of 'widen their timing budget', so in scope.
- Files matching Out-of-Scope globs: 0 (no Out-of-Scope section on this ticket)

Semantic checks:
- Spec stubs run: 0, passed: 0 (none flipped; no .spec/ files touched)
- Contract verification (no Advances: field — test-infrastructure hardening):
  - Named test verifier_test.exs:1681 ('a timeout finding echoes the ExUnit seed'): PASSES. Budget widened 2000 -> @timeout_shim_budget_ms 4000. Covered.
  - Named test review_test.exs:135 ('parses additions and deletions for a tracked file'): PASSES. async: false proven in effect by execution — 'Finished in 4.0 seconds (0.00s async, 4.0s sync)', all 30 tests in the sync phase. FixtureCase honors the option (test_support/specled_ex_fixture_case.ex:5, 'async: Keyword.get(opts, :async, true)'). Covered.
  - Named test verifier_test.exs:1452 ('attribution artifact names embed the OS pid and random entropy'): PASSES, but NOT COVERED by any of the three defenses — see Gaps.
  - Mechanism 'ExUnit.start timeout option': IN EFFECT, proven by execution — probe test asserting ExUnit.configuration()[:timeout] == 120_000 passed. No @tag timeout override is shadowed (only two 5-minute overrides in tracer_incremental_merge_test.exs, both above 120s).
  - Mechanism '@timeout_shim_budget_ms at every family site': TRUE. 7 use sites + 1 definition; the three remaining literals (verifier_test.exs:1042 at 50ms, :1093 at 300ms, :1369 at 50ms) are deliberate short budgets in other families whose assertions require the timeout to fire fast (:1042 asserts 'command exceeded 50ms'), correctly left alone.
- Intent-level scope concerns: none. mix.exs and mix.lock untouched (no new deps); no lib/ change; no .spec/ change.
- Targeted verification: PASS. mix test --include integration on review_test.exs (30 tests, 0 failures), verifier_test.exs + docs_identifier_lint_test.exs (62 tests, 0 failures). mix compile --warnings-as-errors, mix format --check-formatted, mix deps.unlock --check-unused, mix spec.check --no-run-commands (result=pass) all clean.
- Corpus-scoped claims: 6 provenance/config claims validated, 4 by execution. Confirmed true: verification.command_timeout_ms is 400000 in .spec/config.yml; ExUnit's default per-test timeout is 60s; d300c21 did widen this budget 300 -> 2000; c478563 did serialize via async: false including 'use SpecLedEx.FixtureCase, async: false'; SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR exists (lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex:2398); follow-up specled_-td7 exists and its claims are grounded. One falsehood found — see Gaps.
- Full-suite verification: not run by verifier (by design)
- Audit-expanded scope: none

Verdict: FAIL

Gaps:
- verifier_test.exs:1452 gets no effective hardening, yet it is one of the three tests this ticket exists to fix. Measured with --trace: that test runs in 45.9ms. Walking the three defenses against it: (2) the shim-budget widening cannot reach it — it calls run_two_subject_merged with no command_timeout_ms at all, and every diff hunk in verifier_test.exs starts at line 1490, after it; (3) the async: false serialization is applied to review_test.exs only — verifier_test.exs was ALREADY async: false at base c13d1bd (line 3, 'System.put_env PATH shims are VM-global'), so this ticket changes nothing there; (1) the ExUnit 60s -> 120s raise nominally applies suite-wide, but a 45.9ms test reaching the old 60s kill requires roughly a 1300x slowdown, which is not the regime described anywhere on this ticket (the implementer's own synthetic repro was ~2x). The commit message and the IMPLEMENTED comment attribute defense (2) to the :1681 observation and defense (3) to review_test, but neither states what covers :1452 — the omission is not disclosed. Needs either evidence that :1452 is actually covered, or an explicit descope of :1452 with rationale (it is a plausible candidate for the same unexplained class as the docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:255 anomaly already deferred to specled_-td7).
- False claim in the deliverable's own sizing rationale, verifier_test.exs:1490-1498: '@timeout_shim_budget_ms ... Each such test's wall time equals this budget'. Measured per-test with --trace at the 4000ms budget: L#1503 8012ms, L#1537 8011ms, L#1618 8014ms, L#1703 8017ms, L#1783 8014ms (all 2x the budget), L#1562 4033ms, L#1730 4007ms (1x). Five of the seven cost 2x, not 1x, because the merged run's resume pass also times out — which the comment 12 lines below at :1512 states explicitly ('a resume pass runs (and, with this always-hang shim, also times out)'). The file contradicts itself, and this comment is the sole documentation of the runtime trade for anyone tuning the budget later. Fix: say each test costs one or two times this budget depending on whether a resume pass runs.

Notes:
- The aggregate cost figure reported to the ticket ('~20s of bare spec.check runtime') is accurate: measured family total is 48.1s at 4000ms vs ~24.1s at 2000ms, so +24s. Only the per-test comment is wrong, not the headline number.
- Budget headroom is fine and the claim 'the leg's 400s command budget still bounds real hangs' is literally true. Each tagged_tests leg runs a file subset, not the suite (the specled.package leg covers specled_ex_test.exs, docs_identifier_lint_test.exs, index_state_test.exs), and the heaviest file measured is verifier_test.exs at ~50s. Second-order trade worth knowing: a genuinely hung test now consumes 120s of the 400s leg budget instead of 60s.
- The docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:255 observation added to this ticket by the 2026-07-26T03:32:41Z comment is not addressed by the diff. Deferral to specled_-td7 is honestly disclosed and well-reasoned (no forensics were ever captured; the two tests bracketing line 255 are pure-constant assertions), so this is advisory, not a Gap — but it does mean the flake class is not closed by this commit.
- mix spec.check --no-run-commands reports result=pass with no Spec-Drift trailer in stdout; the 'Spec-Drift: test_only' the implementer referenced is the commit-message trailer on d032ff0, which is present and correct.

title: Load-fragile tagged_tests leg: verifier_test.exs:1452/:1681 and review_test.exs:135 intermittently fail under machine load
